newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiei sells share holdings due to poor earnings.
newsitem.headline: Daiei sells share holdings due to poor earnings.

text.p: Daiei Inc said on Friday that it had sold off 20 billion yen worth of its share holdings due to poor earnings for the current business year to March 31, 1997.

The supermarket-chain operator's weak performance is mainly due to sluggish sales of food products in light of the recent O-157 food poisoning epidemic and costs related to restructuring in its group companies.

Daiei did not disclose its latest earnings forecast for the current fiscal year. Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that the company's parent current profit for the half year ended on August 31 would likely have declined 40 percent from a year earlier to slightly less than seven billion yen.
"Revenues from the share sales will be used for our restructuring efforts as well as to cover sluggish earnings," a spokesman for the company said.

Of the total revenue of about 20 billion yen from selling off its stock holdings, Daiei sold in late August about 80 percent of shares it holds in major Japanese department store Takashimaya Co Ltd worth 14 billion yen to Printemps Ginza SA.
Printemps Ginza, which runs a department store in central Tokyo, is also a Daiei group company.

The rest of the revenues were from selling part of Daiei's stock holdings in five banks, including Tokai Bank Ltd, Sanwa Bank Ltd and Sakura Bank Ltd, through which it does most of its financial transactions.
